issue_context.title: Missing Arguments for History Template Functions
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
We can call 
```
self.History[TradeBar](self.symbol, datetime(2021, 5, 1), datetime(2021, 5, 4), Resolution.Minute, extendedMarket=True)
```
without error.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
We get
> During the algorithm initialization, the following exception has occurred: Trying to dynamically access a method that does not exist throws a TypeError exception. To prevent the exception, ensure each parameter type matches those required by the 'int'>) method. Please checkout the API documentation.
  at Initialize
    history = self.History[TradeBar](self.symbol in main.py: line 10
 No method matches given arguments for History: (<class 'QuantConnect.Symbol'>, <class 'datetime.datetime'>, <class 'datetime.datetime'>, <class 'int'>)

But we can use
```
self.History(self.symbol, datetime(2021, 5, 1), datetime(2021, 5, 4), Resolution.Minute, extendedMarket=True)
```
without error.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
N/A

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
https://www.quantconnect.com/terminal/processCache?request=embedded_backtest_b1047f9d35eeeb1aa8580f764e31869b.html

#### System Information
<!--- Required for Bugs. Include any system specific information, such as OS. -->
QC Cloud

comments:
It seems there are missing overloads in the C# API:

```csharp
IEnumerable<TradeBar> History(Symbol symbol, DateTime start, DateTime end, Resolution? resolution = null, 
    bool? fillForward = null, bool? extendedMarket = null, DataMappingMode? dataMappingMode = null,
    DataNormalizationMode? dataNormalizationMode = null, int? contractDepthOffset = null);
    
IEnumerable<T> History<T>(Symbol symbol, DateTime start, DateTime end, Resolution? resolution = null, 
    bool? fillForward = null, bool? extendedMarket = null, DataMappingMode? dataMappingMode = null,
    DataNormalizationMode? dataNormalizationMode = null, int? contractDepthOffset = null);

IEnumerable<DataDictionary<T>> History<T>(IEnumerable<Symbol> symbols, DateTime start, DateTime end, 
    Resolution? resolution = null, bool? fillForward = null, bool? extendedMarket = null, 
    DataMappingMode? dataMappingMode = null, DataNormalizationMode? dataNormalizationMode = null,
    int? contractDepthOffset = null);
```

The same applies to other arguments such as `fillForward`. 
I'd like to use `self.History[TradeBar](symbol, start, end, resolution, fillForward=True)` but got the same error as describe by @DerekMelchin .
